I Never rested on the Muses bed,
Nor dipt my pen in Poesy's well;
But to thee, Drummond, I dedicate
This humble verse, which I hope may tell

That I have sought, in humble imitation,
To catch the spirit of thy song;
And if I fail, I hope my heart's intention
May make amends for all that's wrong.

Thy verses, Drummond, have been my guide,
And I have learned from thee to write;
But if my lines are weak, and my ideas wide,
I hope thou wilt not think it quite unright.

For I am but a humble poet,
Who seeks to learn from those above;
And if I fail, I hope my heart's devotion
May make amends for all that's love.

So here I leave this humble offering,
In hope that thou wilt take it kind;
And if it pleases thee, I shall be blessing,
And if it displeases, I shall be blind.

Thus ends my humble verse, which I dedicate
To thee, Drummond, with all my heart;
And I shall strive, with all my might and energy,
To write like thee, and make my art.
